cards.title: Live 11 mixing and routing
cards.summary: Use track, return and master routing deliberately; inspect the signal path before changing gain or processing.
cards.boundary: Explains controls and routing; does not supply universal balance or loudness targets.

cards.title: Live 11 audio effects: dynamics and tone
cards.summary: Consult native parameter meanings and detector options before applying compression, equalization or limiting.
cards.boundary: Control semantics only; proposed settings remain material-dependent and need a bounced comparison.

cards.title: Live 11 audio effects: depth and space
cards.summary: Use effect parameters and return routing as the basis for designing controlled delays and reverberant depth.
cards.boundary: Do not infer an artist's reverb settings from the manual or equate width with quality.

cards.title: Gain staging from recording to mix
cards.summary: Manage levels through the whole signal chain so one processor does not unintentionally overload the next.
cards.boundary: Suggested working levels are starting points, not a rule for every floating-point signal path or plugin.

cards.title: Pigments downloads and versioned manuals
cards.applies_to: Match the manual to the locally installed version; page currently lists 7.0.1
cards.summary: Locate the versioned manual before designing patches; verify local rendering rather than assuming the latest download is installed.
cards.boundary: No automatic update, purchase, licensing claim or assumption of host compatibility.

cards.title: Offline plugin host and compatibility
cards.summary: Some plugins require particular processing/reset behavior. Test the selected build with a bounded stimulus and retain silent or failed outcomes.
cards.boundary: An offline host result is not native Ableton compatibility or a complete preset test.

cards.title: RUFUS DU SOL: production discussion
cards.authority: Tape Notes interview with the producers
cards.applies_to: Discussion of Inhale / Exhale; Pressure, Fire / Desire, Exhale
cards.summary: The producers discuss vocal distortion, gating and choosing bass parts. Useful starting examples for texture and arrangement decisions.
cards.boundary: Interview summary and gear mentions only; no measured reference audio, exact settings, current popularity rank or instruction to imitate every track.

cards.title: Diva synthesis modules and tutorials
cards.applies_to: Match installed Diva build; site currently lists1.4.8
cards.summary: Use the documented oscillator, filter and envelope modules as building blocks for original bass, lead and pad patches.
cards.boundary: Feature documentation does not establish license state, exact artist patches or local rendering compatibility.

cards.title: Acid V guided sound design and resources
cards.applies_to: Acid V; match manual to installed version
cards.summary: Vendor tutorials cover bass, trance and ambient patch design, including filter sweeps and built-in distortion.
cards.boundary: A tutorial is a design reference. A silent default-state offline probe does not prove the plugin cannot work in Live.

cards.title: Audio timing and warp modes
cards.summary: Inspect warp mode and timing behavior before changing loops.
cards.boundary: Timing and pitch operations are native Live methods; this bridge does not automate them.

cards.title: Sampler instruments and slicing
cards.summary: Consult sampling-instrument modes, envelopes and slicing controls before mapping a sample.
cards.boundary: Availability depends on Live edition. No native device loading or slice-to-MIDI automation is claimed.

cards.title: Arrangement editing and fades
cards.summary: Use clip boundaries, selections and fades deliberately when preparing edits.
cards.boundary: The file editor supports a small subset; native arrangement automation remains outside this connector.

cards.title: Creative strategies and variation
cards.applies_to: General creative workflow; consult applicable tool version
cards.summary: A source for exercises on attributes, variation, automation and arranging.
cards.boundary: The workflow suggestions in this tool are authored prompts, not copied book text or proof of an artist technique.

cards.title: Limiter output and gain comparison
cards.applies_to: General creative workflow; consult applicable tool version
cards.summary: Consult output-level and comparison controls when evaluating limiting.
cards.boundary: This tool does not load or emulate Pro-L 2. Its profiles are independently authored starting points.

cards.title: Creating Melodies 1: Contour
cards.authority: Ableton / Dennis DeSantis official production guide
cards.applies_to: Authored electronic melody; general compositional guidance
cards.summary: Balance rising and falling motion, steps and leaps. Establish a recognizable phrase before developing a contrasting answer; resolve a leap with a step when it serves the phrase.
cards.boundary: Practical compositional suggestions, not an empirical guarantee of catchiness or a substitute for listening.

cards.title: Syncopation, Body-Movement and Pleasure in Groove Music
cards.authority: Witek et al. 2014, PLOS ONE; primary listener experiment
cards.applies_to: Ratings of the tested synthesized funk drum-break stimuli
cards.summary: In the tested drum breaks, medium syncopation received the highest movement and pleasure ratings. Preserve a readable pulse and choose a few displacement points rather than maximizing density.
cards.boundary: Production suggestion is an inference, not a universal target. The 2015 correction (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0139409) fixes stimulus indexing/transcripts; authors state findings and interpretations are unchanged.

cards.title: Uncertainty and Surprise Jointly Predict Musical Pleasure
cards.authority: Cheung et al. 2019, Current Biology; primary paper on author website
cards.applies_to: Behavioral and fMRI experiments on Western tonal chord expectancy
cards.summary: Pleasure depended on the interaction of prospective uncertainty and retrospective surprise, rather than a rule to maximize surprise. A production inference is to establish a phrase and reserve a deliberate contrast or cadence.
cards.boundary: The experiment concerns chords and expectancy, not a validated algorithm for writing melodies, genre authenticity, preset selection or mix quality. Listener taste remains individual.

cards.title: Drop It: The Kick in Electronic Music
cards.applies_to: Electronic kick design; named tools require installed edition/version
cards.summary: Treat attack, body and tail as separate kick roles. A short transient and a long low body can demand different arrangement space.
cards.boundary: No universal kick preset, fundamental or decay time. The article does not establish that any named effect is available through this MCP.

cards.title: Enter the Temple of Boom: Acoustic Kicks
cards.summary: When combining drum sources, check their combined timing and polarity rather than choosing each in isolation.
cards.boundary: A polarity flip is not arbitrary phase alignment. A level or correlation metric cannot choose the best drum sound; numerical tests supplement later audition.

cards.title: Make basslines
cards.summary: Bass supports harmony and can relate to or contrast with the drums rhythmically.
cards.boundary: No promise that a root-only pattern or any frequency target makes a convincing bass line. Choose phrase rhythm and register musically.

cards.title: Backbeats
cards.summary: Snare/clap on beats two and four is a common backbeat; four-on-the-floor kick is one contrasting vocabulary.
cards.boundary: These are examples, not mandatory genre templates. A sparse or halftime section can intentionally depart from them.

cards.title: Using Grooves
cards.summary: Groove timing, velocity, randomization and quantization are separate controls; extracted grooves can retain a source timing pattern.
cards.boundary: Native Groove Pool/extraction are manual here. Randomizing every voice is not a validated substitute for intentional groove; no native extraction was executed.

cards.title: Instrument, Drum and Effect Racks
cards.summary: Chains in the same choke group silence one another when triggered; useful for open/closed hat behavior.
cards.boundary: Choke groups and rack chains are not exposed by the current native bridge. Offline sample gating must be authored explicitly.

cards.title: Side chain compression
cards.authority: FabFilter / Maarten de Boer original educational article
cards.applies_to: General compressor detector principles, not a required plugin
cards.summary: A separate detector source can control bass level when the kick hits. Very fast timing may distort slow bass waveforms.
cards.boundary: Choose recovery for the actual bass phrase; this source is not an installation claim, preset or universal millisecond target. File-envelope ducking is distinct from a native compressor.

cards.title: Live11 delay and reverb control reference
cards.summary: Tempo-sync delay divisions, feedback/filtering, reverb predelay/decay and Utility polarity are distinct documented controls.
cards.boundary: Consult exact device semantics before native edits. Private offline filtered delays/reverb do not prove native routing, plugin equivalence or perceptual mix quality.

cards.title: Dramatic Arc
cards.authority: Ableton / Dennis DeSantis official production guide
cards.applies_to: Original arrangements at multiple time scales
cards.summary: Introduce material, build tension, reach a climax and release it. Texture and density changes can shape this progression.
cards.boundary: An authored arrangement strategy, not an empirical guarantee or automatic song-generation endpoint. Contrast should be audible in material, not labels alone.
